utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Grandma Stiepel.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Who? What's my name?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Grandma Stiepel.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Grandma Stiepel? Here, let's turn the piano up. And you want to play piano for Grandma Stiepel? How old are you, Kaya?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: 12. Oh, that's pretty. So what I really need to do is get my hands— especially this hand is very— This finger is twisted because it's got arthritis in it, so I have to start using it.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Right, and it's good to play piano just for that purpose, just to use it, and just playing that 5 fingers.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah, that will help a lot.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Right, and if you— that's a good exercise, Grandma. If you want to make that exercise even more extended a little— Uh-huh. Okay, so you see how— okay, here's how you play C, D, E, F, G, and then just move your hand up.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, one more over.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: One more over and do the same thing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's good exercise.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: So that you can move up, and then when you come backwards, you can come backwards starting with pinky. Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah, well, that's what I need is to get my hands limbered up.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Great. You want to try that?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay, then just move up. Just move up one.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, just move up one?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Move your thumb. Thumb. And then start here now.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Right, and then move up. Use yourself. Uh-huh. Right. There you go. Now you can go as high as you want, then start coming backwards. Start with your pinky, wherever you're at. And then move your pinky down one.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: My pinky? Oh yeah, next time it's my pinky.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: And then you won't get so bored just doing it in one spot.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You just travel up and down the piano.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'll do that. I'll practice that a lot. Because then I think it's so much easier after you get your hands where you can move them.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. It's a good warm-up. So for your right hand, and you can do the same thing with your left hand if you want to warm your left hand up. Same pattern, same way. And then just move up.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Just move the thumb up. No, this one, you have to start back here.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Right. And you know what that also does? It kind of gives you a little bit more familiarity with the rest of the piano.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay, so Grandma, show me the variation now of that where you play 2 on each one. 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2. Do you like that, Grandma?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Do you like it? You look like you're concentrating.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah it's fun.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It is, isn't it? Yeah. Did I tell you what my new product is called? I'm calling it my 'Boot Camp' series.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Boot camp? Why on earth would you call it that? I'm not enlisting in the army, I'm just trying to play 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'!

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Oh, no! hhhh It's just a name people use now for intense training sessions. You know, like a fitness class. I'm calling the specific one 'Boot Camp for Clumsy Fingers.'

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, that's funny hhhh. Well, as long as I don't have to do any push-ups on the keys!
